Topics · One God, one message

Did the Buddha point to what is never born?

The Quran agrees that what begins is not its own source, and speaks of what does not begin.

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْإِنسَـٰنِ حِينٌ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُن شَيْـًٔا مَّذْكُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Has there [not] come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] mentioned?

Quran · Al-Insan 76:1

Translation

what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him? For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor. You make him ruler over the works of your hands. You have put all things under his feet:

Original · Hebrew

מָֽה־אֱנ֥וֹשׁ כִּֽי־תִזְכְּרֶ֑נּוּ וּבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם כִּ֣י תִפְקְדֶֽנּוּ׃ וַתְּחַסְּרֵ֣הוּ מְּ֭עַט מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכָב֖וֹד וְהָדָ֣ר תְּעַטְּרֵֽהוּ׃ תַּ֭מְשִׁילֵהוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣י יָדֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֝ל שַׁ֣תָּה תַֽחַת־רַגְלָֽיו׃

the Psalms · 8:4-6

World English Bible

Begin from something nobody disputes: you are a thing that arose. There was a time when you were not mentioned anywhere, and then you were. In the Buddha's account, whatever arises is made and conditioned. If everything that arises is conditioned, is there any way out of the conditions? The Udana reports the Buddha saying that if there were no unconditioned, no escape from the conditioned could be known.

A question for you

When you look at anything that arises, yourself included, what does it depend on?

If you sayCauses and conditions, back without end
ThenThat is the Buddha's own picture of the conditioned world: a chain without a beginning. The next verses set something beside it: what stands before every beginning.
If you saySomething that does not itself arise
ThenThe Udana reports the Buddha saying this exists. The question then is what can be said of it, which is the subject of the rest of the page.
If you sayI can't say
ThenThe suttas report the Buddha leaving many such questions unanswered. The verses ahead set out what the Quran says, and you weigh it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿هُوَ ٱلْأَوَّلُ وَٱلْـَٔاخِرُ وَٱلظَّـٰهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He is the First[1623] and the Last,[1624] the Ascendant[1625] and the Intimate,[1626] and He is, of all things, Knowing.

Translator's notes

[1623] Before whom nothing existed. Also, He who is supreme, foremost or uppermost. [1624] Enduring eternally when nothing else remains. [1625] Nothing being above Him. Another meaning is "the Apparent," i.e., evident through His creation and revelation. [1626] Nothing being nearer than Him by way of His knowledge. Another meaning is "the Unapparent," i.e., concealed from man's physical senses.

Quran · Al-Hadid 57:3

Translation

This is what Yahweh, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, Yahweh of Armies, says: “I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no God.

Original · Hebrew

כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃

Isaiah · 44:6

World English Bible

The verse uses one word for what comes before every beginning: the First. Set it beside the Buddha's line: unborn, not traced to a cause. The verse goes on to name the First and to add that it knows all things. The two meet at one point: there is something that does not itself arise. What more is said of it comes next.

A question for you

Which claim would you test first: that there is an unconditioned, or that it knows?

If you sayThat there is an unconditioned
ThenThe Buddha affirms this claim and the Quran affirms it. It is a meeting place, and what comes after it is where to look.
If you sayThat it knows
ThenThis is what the Quran says. The next verses show how the Quran describes it, and you weigh the description.
If you sayNeither yet
ThenThat fits the Buddha's way of testing: accept nothing before you have checked. The Quran suggests a similar test elsewhere.

Part 3 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ١ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ٢ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ٣ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,[2011] Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.[2012] He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

Translator's notes

[2011] Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds.

[2012] He who is absolute, perfect, complete, essential, self-sufficient and sufficient to meet the needs of all creation; the one eternally and constantly required and sought, depended upon by all existence and to whom all matters will ultimately return.

Quran · Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4

Translation

Yahweh will be King over all the earth. In that day Yahweh will be one, and his name one.

Original · Hebrew

וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶחָ֖ד וּשְׁמ֥וֹ אֶחָֽד׃

Zechariah · 14:9

World English Bible

This is the Quran's shortest description of the One: one, turned to by everything while turning to nothing, neither giving birth nor born, with nothing like it. Place it beside the Buddha's word: what has no beginning. What the texts share is plain: no birth, and nothing before it. The chapter goes on to name the One who is turned to. How far do you go with it? That is yours to say.

A question for you

Where do you stop?

If you sayAt the unconditioned, with nothing more said
ThenThat is where many Buddhists stand, with great care. The chapter goes on to name the One, and that is yours to weigh in your own time.
If you sayAt one who is known and turned to
ThenThat is what the chapter says. If you arrive there, ask what follows, which is the subject of the questions after this.
If you sayI am still weighing
ThenThat is the honest place to be. The Quran itself leaves the door open to reflection, and the next questions wait whenever you want them.

The same in the other books
